thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: High 5xx spike detected on hosted inference across us-west-2; error rate ~12% over 5m for /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Paging oncall.

sara (oncall): on it. grabbing graphs now. any customer-facing alerts sent?

kelsey (support): not yet, we're seeing several escalations from 2 customers — starting triage thread with them. some requests show long tail latency + OOMs in logs.

jhansen: saw continuous-batching worker queues filling then timeouts. suspect a change in request size distribution + a model with heavier kv-cache memory causing backpressure.

ops-bot: ran quick check: GPUs at 92% mem, 85% util on some nodes; autoscaler hasn't provisioned more capacity due to reserved pool thresholds.

sara (oncall): plan: 1) immediate traffic shaping to reduce tail 5xx 2) increase batching buffer/time to absorb spikes (trade latency for throughput) 3) disable reranking endpoint for non-enterprise routes as temporary mitigation. agree?

mike (next-oncall): +1 to mitigation. add quota bump/limits for enterprise customers if they can tolerate. track metrics after each step.

jhansen: i'll own the batching change. setting continuous batching timeout from 10ms -> 80ms and max_batch_size from 32 -> 64 for the affected models. this should allow larger aggregated batches and reduce per-token overhead. we'll accept ~30-60ms extra tail latency.

sara (oncall): do it. post the exact command you run so we can roll back. also add a temporary route-level rate limit for free-tier to 5rps.

jhansen: running now:

```
# increase batching window and batch size for text-generation model group
redwoodctl update-routing --route /v1/generate --model-group rwd-text-32k \
  --set batching.continuous=true \
  --set batching.timeout_ms=80 \
  --set batching.max_batch_size=64

# and for chat route
redwoodctl update-routing --route /v1/chat --set batching.timeout_ms=80 --set batching.max_batch_size=64
```

ops-bot: applying config via control-plane, rolling to 20% of pods for canary.

incident-bot: :hourglass_flowing_sand: Apply started (change-id: cb-20240418-01). Monitoring metrics.

kelsey (support): contacting the two complaining customers to let them know we're mitigating and we may introduce slightly higher latency but lower errors.

sara (oncall): also temporarily enable route-level quota enforcement for non-paid plans:

```
redwoodctl set-quota --route /v1/generate --plan free --rps 5 --burst 10
```
This will shed some load quickly.

mike (next-oncall): i'll prepare a queue backpressure dashboard and watch tail latency. notify if p95 > 800ms.

jhansen: canary looks good on pod logs: worker queue depth dropped ~40%, 5xx dropped from 12% -> 4% in canary. expanding to 100% now.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Change cb-20240418-01 promoted to 100% (completed).

ops-bot: also disabled reranking for public routes as requested:

```
redwoodctl feature-toggle set reranker --scope public --enabled false --note "mitigation: reduce heavy CPU/KV loads"
```

kelsey (support): customers updated — one said errors are gone, the other sees slight latency increase but acceptable.

sara (oncall): OK good. next: apply soft rate-limits on new-session creation to protect cold-starts. adding a traffic-shaper rule to delay new session requests when backend queue depth > 1000 to keep system stable.

jhansen: implemented traffic-shaper rule in Envoy route config to add a 200ms stagger when queue depth threshold exceeded. Also tuned per-model cache eviction to free KV memory sooner for large context models.

mike (next-oncall): i'm taking handoff; sara, anything to flag?

sara (oncall): handoff: system stable but still ~2% elevated errors on a subset of long-context requests. mitigation actions summary: increased batching timeout -> 80ms, max_batch_size 64, disabled reranker for public routes, free-tier rps 5, traffic-shaper for new sessions. Monitor p95 and 5xx for the next 2 hours.

mike (next-oncall): ack. i'll run hourly checks and coordinate with infra if autoscaler needs tuning.

jhansen: note for postmortem: investigate why autoscaler didn't react earlier (threshold config) and why model memory growth coincided with request pattern change. also propose a feature: adaptive batching that increases timeout only when queue depth suggests sustained load, to avoid latency hit on normal traffic.

sara (oncall): adding follow-up tasks to /incidents/retrospective board. CS to follow up with impacted customers and offer usage credit.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident cb-20240418-01 mitigations applied, severity reduced. Thread closed for active paging. Please open a postmortem doc if follow-ups required.

ops-bot: snapshot of commands/configs applied saved to /ops/changes/cb-20240418-01 for audit.

kelsey (support): thanks everyone. will keep customers updated. :thumbsup:

mike (next-oncall): taking over monitoring. if anything flares, call me @mike.

sara (oncall): ty team. good work triaging. will sync tomorrow on RCA. :coffee:
